description:
## Status

Invalid and superseded by the accepted recalculator model. The parked commit `77f87512c` added per-answer derivation identities, read watermarks, and standing-derivation clones, but no production consumer used that precision. Its own measurements reported 6–10% more wall-clock work, and job-wide waits erased the claimed cleanliness benefit.

`fz-tfn.59` subsequently deleted the dormant per-derivation publisher substrate. Restoring this branch would recreate a second ownership/cleanliness authority and directly contradict the epic's one-job publisher identity, exact edge-triggered work, and less-work requirements.

## Preserved evidence

- A finer ledger without a consumer is negative value: it adds traffic and storage while changing no answer.
- Read-prefix watermarks are not semantic support for individual alternatives and cannot retract a self-supporting recursive value.
- Job-wide waiting collapses per-answer finality, so the proposed representation did not make cycles ordinarily reactive.
- The parked implementation was 1,018 additions / 64 deletions across nine files and measured +6–10% wall time.

No code from `wt/kdt132-watermarks` should be restored. The valid requirement—content-specific support before aggregate joins erase it—is owned by the corrected `fz-tfn` source/publication cutovers, with a real `ReturnType`/`ActivationInputs` consumer and a bounded termination proof required before landing.

The obsolete remote branch is deleted after this description records why it was rejected. There was no PR to close.
title: Invalid: per-answer watermarks add work without semantic support
